nodes.label: Pinned Server Identity Changed
nodes.rationale: An unexpected identity can mean MITM, wrong address, lost server state, or deliberate replacement. There is no automatic insecure override: the operator must explicitly forget and re-pair or import a managed replacement pin.

nodes.label: Create-Once Administration Lock Files
nodes.rationale: User administration, identity installation, and client trust updates use create-once lock files so concurrent writers cannot lose each other's changes; a killed process can leave .users.lock, .identity.lock, or .trusted-servers.lock behind and only a verified-stale lock may be removed.

nodes.label: Slow Directory Listing Diagnosis
nodes.rationale: A fast first ls followed by a ~30 s stall on an immediate second ls identifies the old mismatched child-metadata TTL, which caused a per-child GetMetadata wave that outlived the directory view. Raising --callback-timeout-ms only hides symptoms; --max-directory-entry-tasks (default 64) can hurt a saturated rotational array.

nodes.label: End-to-End Callback Timeout Budget
nodes.rationale: --callback-timeout-ms is one 120 s absolute budget covering the initial request, connection replacement, reconnect backoff, reauthentication, handle reopening/lock replay, and a safe retry; no phase restarts it, and the callback bridge adds only a fixed 100 ms margin to deliver the typed result. A stalled connection generation is marked unhealthy so later demand does not reselect it, and a shared reconnect outlives the waiter that started it because it remains useful to others. Idempotent exhaustion maps to ETIMEDOUT; an ambiguous mutation maps to EIO and is never retried.
